Q776.L1t: The passage is a news-style obituary describing the long marriage, family life and community work of Helen and Kenneth Felumlee.
Q776.L2t: Kenneth retired in 1983, after which the couple used their free time to travel by bus through almost every US state.
Q776.L3t: The passage says Kenneth worked as a railroad car inspector, as a mechanic, and as a mail carrier for the Post Office, and that he also served as a Sunday teacher at church, so you can count each distinct role it names.
Q776.L4t: Kenneth held four different jobs or roles: railroad car inspector, mechanic, mail carrier and Sunday school teacher.
Q776.L2f: Kenneth and Helen eloped in Newport on Feb. 20, 1994, after knowing each other for only a few weeks.
Q776.L3f: Working as an inspector and as a mechanic on the railroad was a single job, and teaching Sunday school was unpaid church volunteering, so only the railroad work and the mail carrier post count as his jobs.
Q776.L4f: Kenneth had just a pair of jobs, working on the railroad and then delivering mail.

Q813.L1t: The passage is a travel-style guide to several converted-factory art districts in Chinese cities, giving their addresses and opening hours.
Q813.L2t: Redtory was opened as an art district in 2009, though its buildings date back to a can factory built in 1956.
Q813.L3t: The passage dates the start of each art district: Guangzhou in 2009, Chongqing in the early 2000s, and Shanghai with its first studio in 2002, whereas artists began moving into the Beijing factory buildings in 2001.
Q813.L4t: The Beijing district at the 798 factory is the earliest of the four, since artists started moving in there in 2001, before the others.
Q813.L2f: Redtory was built in the 1990s as a textile mill and is located on the bank of Suzhou Creek.
Q813.L3f: The textile factory on Moganshan Road stopped production in 1999 and was turned into an art district right away, which is earlier than any of the other three districts.
Q813.L4f: The Moganshan Road art district in Shanghai was the first of the four to be built.

Q838.L1t: The passage is an essay about medical ethics and honesty in professional practice.
Q838.L2t: The passage notes that other professions, such as law and government, also face situations where deception seems to avoid serious consequences.
Q838.L3t: The passage opens by asking whether doctors should ever lie to patients, uses a cancer patient as its example, and then argues that truthful information helps patients cope, so it urges open debate over the doctor's choice between telling and hiding the truth.
Q838.L4t: The passage is mainly about whether doctors should tell patients the truth about their illness.
Q838.L2f: Most doctors in the studies mentioned say that seriously ill patients always demand to know every detail of their condition.
Q838.L3f: The passage's central aim is to set two conflicting sets of research findings side by side and to call for more investigation, since it offers no view on what doctors should do.
Q838.L4f: The passage is mainly about whether more studies should be carried out on this subject.
